correctness.rationale: Every binary linear k-subspace has a unique reduced-row-echelon basis; pivot sets and all rightward nonpivot free entries are exhaustively enumerated. Each of its 2^k words is checked for all distinct length-(n-1) deletion outputs with exact integer incidence tallies. Replayed verifier counts all k-max subspaces for 1<=n<=9, all excluded (k+1)-subspaces for 2<=n<=9, and all 6347715 [10,7] subspaces, with zero forbidden pass. Every higher-dimensional code contains a forbidden subcode. The explicit rank-six length-ten generator has (220,232,60) one-deletion-list histogram. All boundary conditions, n=1 and duplicate positions included. No infinite claim is made.

value.rationale: The October 2026 generalized half-Singleton work calls out binary list decoding as exceptional. The exact finite invariant K_2(n), not just code-size recomputation, locates the first blocklength at which a binary linear two-list one-deletion scheme can carry six information bits: n=9 fails despite the rate-2/3 equality benchmark, n=10 succeeds. The full initial profile gives a natural sharp benchmark for linear synchronization codes, with finite exhaustive proof and an explicit construction. This precise cutoff is motivated by the source gap, is not implied by its inequalities, and requires no speculative downstream theorem.
